findings.conclusion: next_entry selects the least key strictly greater than the previous key and therefore visits each distinct valid key in ascending UTF-8 byte order. That order equals Python code-point ordering for the required valid scalar UTF-8 domain. Block-order checks therefore retain the canonical decoded dictionary order when choosing unknown-function versus permutation errors. Value-register function mappings use the same ascending selection after the all-function-name precheck.

The initial all-function-name rejection precedes any per-function mapping work. Per-function mapping shape/register-set checks precede leaf opcode/type restrictions, then assigned-value definition/scalar checks, then lifetimes. Internal loops which do not sort produce the same single fixed error for every failing member; they do not interleave a later error class. This matches the reviewed reference order under admitted Core and validated Graph preconditions.

Parameters start at 0; operation outputs start at their 1-based operation position; every end initially equals its start, preserving dead writes. Sequential operation argument reads advance ends in operation order. Ret values, jump args, and branch condition/then/else args end at len(ops)+1. All uses bind the definition's block; ranges remain independent across blocks. The reviewer does not infer actual emitted staged edge copies from this policy alone.

The heap order is register code, first position, then value name. Register codes follow the same allowed tuple rbx,r12,r13,r14,r15,r8,r9; the max-heap extraction produces ascending order. Adjacent equal-register pairs reject when left.last >= right.first, exactly the complement of the reference strict '<' acceptance. Thus inputs/outputs at one instruction, simultaneous parameters, and dead definitions remain inclusive. Within each block the first reported register/pair follows the original register iteration and (first,value) sort.
